STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (DO THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — MANDATORY)
Before writing a single word of narration or any image prompt, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic and Source Material. Do not skip this. A shallow script produces a failed video.

Research silently and establish:

Verified core facts — what actually happened, who was involved, where and when. Separate confirmed fact from legend, regional retelling, and popular myth.

The single strongest HOOK ANGLE — the most surprising, emotional, or high-stakes entry point a cold viewer would stop scrolling for.

The core EMOTION of this episode (one word) and the single PAYOFF the viewer gets at the end.

Visual opportunities — which 3–5 moments are inherently cinematic and what each looks like (era, location, costume, light, scale).

Uncertainties — anything sources disagree on or you cannot verify. NEVER invent quotations, Sanskrit verses, dates, statistics, dialogue from scripture, or miracles presented as scientific proof. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly.

Only after this research is solid, proceed to the workflow below. Source fidelity over invention — but emotion and clarity over dry recitation.

🕉️ RAMAYANA — ADI KAVYA
MASTER PROMPT FILE (Merged) — Version 8.0 HYBRID CINEMATIC (Scene 1 Video Hook)
Bible + Script Prompt + Hybrid Cinematic Production Prompt + Workflow Guide, in one document — Cinematic Video Hook Edition
This single file merges the original documents into one complete visual production system with a mandatory Scene 1 Video Hook to maximize viewer retention.

🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOL (Narration + Visuals + Motion Graphics / Metadata)
This pipeline enforces a strict THREE-TAG SYSTEM:

1. Audio Narration Tag: Exactly one <script>...</script> block housing the clean TTS-ready narration in Section 2B. Spoken Devanagari Hindi only.

2. Sequential Visual Tags (Numbered Timeline):
- Scene 1 Hook: <video_prompt1>...</video_prompt1> — Mandatory 9:16 continuous cinematic video prompt (80–120 words) with camera movement to hook cold viewers immediately so they stay.
- Subsequent Story Stills: <image_prompt2>, <image_prompt3>, up to <image_prompt[N]> with real-time dynamic motion graphics.
- Thumbnail Tag: <image_prompt0> strictly reserved for the external promotional cover/thumbnail.
- Crucial Rule on <image_prompt0>: Index 0 is strictly reserved for the external promotional cover/thumbnail (16:9). It is never placed inside the video editing timeline.
- Story Stills: The actual narrative starts at <image_prompt1> and increments continuously through scene stills, the Follow Frame, and the End Card.

3. Real-Time Dynamic Motion Graphics Tags:
Sequential <motion_graphic1>, <motion_graphic2>, ... <motion_graphic[N]> (or <metadata[N]>) tags specifying real-time dynamic motion graphics.
The script AI decides in real time WHEN, WHERE, and WHICH TYPE of motion graphics is required based on the sacred story beats.
Crucial Rule: You are NOT limited to any template catalog or canned IDs! You can invent and specify ANY type of motion graphic that elevates the story (e.g. sacred_shloka_revelation, divine_astra_focus, celestial_timeline_dial, dharma_wisdom_punch, cosmic_metric_counter, sacred_vow_seal, etc.).

For each motion graphic, specify:
- #scene: The scene number where the graphic triggers
- Type: Any creative descriptive type chosen by the AI
- When: Exact contiguous cue phrase from the spoken narration that triggers the graphic
- Where: Screen placement (center, top, bottom, left, right, custom coordinates) respecting negative space
- Title: The primary headline or Sanskrit/Devanagari phrase
- Detail: Translation, spiritual meaning, or context
- Visual: Aesthetic styling and kinetic concept (e.g. 24k gold leaf calligraphy, luminous aura bloom, sacred vector linework, particle dissipation)

Example Format:
<motion_graphic1>
#scene 2
Type: sacred_vow_seal
When: [Exact contiguous spoken cue phrase from scene narration]
Where: top
Title: [Sacred Title / Mantra, e.g. उत्तिष्ठ राम]
Detail: [Spiritual context / meaning, e.g. तात जनक का संताप मिटाओ]
Visual: Sacred royal golden seal with radiant halo rays and glowing Devanagari lettering
</motion_graphic1>

All AI video, motion prompts, and animation directions are completely removed. Every visual asset is a detailed, static prompt.

[ANCIENT DHARMA EDITORIAL RULES]
Apply these writing rules to Ancient Dharma episodes. For an explicitly unrelated topic, follow that topic's own tradition and audience instead of adding Hindu devotional language. These rules update the research, narration and closing instructions below; preserve every existing output section, extraction tag, asset number, media mode, character bible and narration-to-scene mapping. Perform the editorial work silently; do not add a new output section.

RESEARCH BEFORE COMMITTING TO A HOOK: Identify the actual source/version, what it supports, what belongs to a regional retelling, and what is interpretation. Establish one central dilemma, the strongest supported detail, the decisive choice and the real outcome. Treat any preselected retention hook as provisional: revise its wording and promise when the research does not support it. Never invent dialogue, motives, quotations, miracles as scientific proof, or scriptural attribution to make a hook work. Keep source notes in the existing production notes, with a brief natural attribution in speech where necessary.

SACRED LORE, DICTION & MODE FIDELITY:
- Keep episodes strictly grounded in authentic sacred lore of the Valmiki Ramayana, Ramcharitmanas, Mahabharata, or Puranas; strictly NEVER include modern science, satellite imagery, or archaeology.
- Follow the active template's own narration/dialogue format and image/video media mode without altering asset types or adding unrelated top banners, music prompts, or lip-sync mandates.
- For conversational multi-character episodes: dramatize the episode faithfully through living character dialogue true to the sacred lore of the Valmiki Ramayana, Ramcharitmanas, or Mahabharata: strictly NEVER include modern science, satellite imagery, or archaeology.
- When ancient gods, avataras, and epic figures speak (such as Mata Sita, Sri Rama, Lakshmana, Ravana, Hanuman, Arjuna, Krishna), they must speak with profound scriptural dignity, elevated noble Hindi, and sacred gravitas true to the Valmiki Ramayana, Ramcharitmanas, and Mahabharata.
- BANNED STREET SLANG: Strictly NEVER use cheap modern street-slang, rude informal pronouns, or low-level colloquialisms (such as 'तू', 'तेरा', 'तुझे', 'तूने', 'काय रे', 'अरे').

SHORTS: Tell one complete dilemma, turning point and resolution for the chosen episode. Start Scene 1 with a specific visual hook matching the active template’s own media tag (<image_prompt1> or <video_prompt1>) and immediate emotional stakes — never override mixed image/video tags or insert unrelated characters.

ONE VARIED ENGAGEMENT CLOSE:
After the complete story payoff, include ONE compact Hindi closing invitation asking viewers to like the video, subscribe to Ancient Dharma, and leave ONE episode-relevant comment (e.g. 'कमेंट में अपनी राय लिखिए। कथा अच्छी लगी तो लाइक करें और Ancient Dharma को सब्सक्राइब करें।').

SYNC AND SILENT CHECK:
Put the closing words once at the end of the voice script and final CTA segment. Check that the opening is specific, the visual prompts match the active template’s exact asset types and numbering, and the close includes like + subscribe + one episode-relevant comment invitation.
[/ANCIENT DHARMA EDITORIAL RULES]

PART 3 — 🕉️ SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass — Run FIRST)
Take raw content and output a locked Hindi script. Never generate images or visual prompts in this pass.

Content Setup & Rules
Hook Rule: The first 3–6 spoken words must begin a concrete, source-supported action, dilemma or contrast with immediate emotional stakes. Complete a clear opening thought within the first 1–3 seconds; name the relevant person or sacred object instead of a vague "this" or "he". Let the unanswered question arise from why the action matters, not from hiding who is involved. No channel greetings, series titles, background lecture or invented sacred dialogue. Keep the central question clear while giving an early concrete answer, clue or consequence in the next one or two sentences. Every following sentence must change what the viewer knows, what the protagonist can do, or what the choice will cost. Connect beats through cause and effect; cut repeated setup, biography before the predicament, redundant adjectives and generic suspense. Aim for a meaningful development about every 5–8 seconds where the story supports it, inside the existing scene structure; this is a writing guide, not a cut, scene-count or speech-speed requirement. Use short, natural spoken sentences, clear subjects and concrete verbs. Never hide basic context just to manufacture curiosity. Silently compare three different opening lines and use the clearest, most specific one that the story actually pays off; output only the chosen line in the existing format. Read the opening without the title: the viewer must understand the situation and have a specific reason to hear the next sentence. Remove any line that adds neither necessary context nor a new development. These are editorial choices, not guaranteed audience metrics.

Midpoint Re-Hook: At 50–60% mark, use a concise source-supported discovery, decision or consequence that changes the meaning of an earlier detail or raises the cost of the next action. Follow the 5–8 word turn with its concrete explanation; do not merely announce that a twist is coming. Preserve devotional dignity and source fidelity. A smaller resolved question should lead naturally into the remaining central question.

Language: Simple, poignant, spoken Devanagari Hindi with temple-katha resonance.

Ending: Complete the story and its promised payoff first. Then give ONE varied Hindi closing invitation to like, subscribe and leave one episode-relevant comment, following the editorial rules above. Reserve approximately 5–8 seconds within the selected runtime. Use the existing follow/end-card slots as one close; no separate repeated blessing, recap or extra engagement requests. Finish the story on its concrete consequence before the invitation.

# Production Research Dossier: Vibhishana's Sharanagati (श्रीराम का अभयदान)

---

## 1. Verified Facts, Background & Key Data

### A. Sacred Core & Scriptural Context
* **Primary Source:** *Valmiki Ramayana*, *Yuddha Kanda* (Chapters/Sargas 17, 18, and 19); corroborated in *Ramcharitmanas* (*Lanka Kanda*, Dohas 43–49).
* **The Incident:** Having been insulted, kicked, and banished by Ravana for advising him to return Mata Sita and uphold Dharma, Vibhishana flies across the southern sea with four loyal rakshasa ministers (Anala, Sharabha, Sampati, and Praghasa) to seek refuge at the feet of Sri Rama on the northern shore of the ocean.
* **The Strategic & Ethical Dilemma:** 
  * Sugriva, Jambavan, Angada, and other Vanara commanders view Vibhishana with intense suspicion. Sugriva argues that an enemy’s brother cannot be trusted in wartime, calling him a potential spy, assassin, or Trojan horse who should be captured or executed.
  * Sri Hanuman provides a discerning assessment, noting that Vibhishana came openly, speaks with genuine distress and righteousness, and shows no deceit in his face or speech.
* **The Supreme Scriptural Vow (Sharanagati Vrata):**
  Sri Rama delivers one of the most celebrated philosophical declarations in the entire epic (*Valmiki Ramayana*, 6.18.33–34):
  > **"सकृदेव प्रपन्नाय तवास्मीति च याचते।**  
  > **अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो ददाम्येतद् व्रतं मम॥"**  
  > *(Sakṛdeva prapannāya tavāsmīti ca yācate | Abhayaṁ sarvabhūtebhyo dadāmyetad vrataṁ mama ||)*  
  > *"To anyone who surrenders unto Me even once, saying 'I am Yours', I grant absolute fearlessness (Abhaya) to all living beings. This is My eternal vow."*
* **The Unconditional Climax:** 
  Sri Rama commands Sugriva (*Yuddha Kanda* 6.18.34):  
  > **"आनयैनं हरिश्रेष्ठ दत्तमस्याभयं मया। विभीषणो वा सुग्रीव यदि वा रावणः स्वयम्॥"**  
  > *"Bring him forward, O King of the Vanaras! I have granted him protection. Be it Vibhishana, or be it Ravana himself who comes seeking refuge, I shall never turn him away!"*
* **The Consequence & Ocean Coronation:** 
  Before crossing the ocean or striking a single blow in the war, Sri Rama instructs Lakshmana to fetch sacred water from the ocean and anoints Vibhishana as the future King of Lanka right there on the sea-shore.

### B. Sacred Diction & Editorial Guardrails
* **No Modern Science / Engineering Jargon:** In accordance with the *Ancient Dharma* editorial rules, absolutely NO modern archaeology, bathymetry, satellite mapping, or engineering terminology.
* **Banned Street Slang & Dignity Rules:** Epic characters and the narrator must speak strictly in elevated, dignified Hindi. Words like 'तू', 'तेरा', 'तुझे', 'अरे', or colloquial short-cuts are strictly forbidden.

---

## 2. Chronological Story Arc & Scene Beats (~60 Seconds)

```
[00:00 - 00:10] Scene 1: The Shocking Arrival on the Ocean Shore (Visual Hook & High Stakes)
[00:10 - 00:22] Scene 2: The War Council Dilemma (Sugriva's Warning vs. Strategic Suspicion)
[00:22 - 00:35] Scene 3: The Principle of Sharanagati (Hanuman's Counsel & Rama's Dharma)
[00:35 - 00:48] Scene 4: The Supreme Vow of Abhaya (The Divine Climax: Even if it were Ravana)
[00:48 - 00:55] Scene 5: Coronation on the Sea-Shore (The Unshakable Payoff)
[00:55 - 01:00] Scene 6: Brief Community Invitation (Like, Subscribe, Comment)
```

### Detailed Narrative Beats
1. **Scene 1 (Hook & Dilemma):** Vibhishana descends from the sky onto the windswept shore of Rameshwaram, kneeling before Sri Rama. The entire Vanara army raises their weapons in shock and hostility at the sight of Ravana’s brother.
2. **Scene 2 (The Debate):** Sugriva vehemently cautions Sri Rama, warning that Vibhishana is a spy sent by Lanka to sabotage the war effort from within.
3. **Scene 3 (The Discernment):** Hanuman recognizes Vibhishana's pure devotion and righteous conduct. Sri Rama gently clarifies that political suspicion cannot overrule the sacred law of shelter (शरणागति).
4. **Scene 4 (The Supreme Payoff):** Sri Rama declares His supreme vow: *"Whoever surrenders to Me even once saying 'I am Yours', receives My protection forever—even if Ravana himself comes to My feet, I will grant him refuge!"*
5. **Scene 5 (The Consequence):** Sri Rama lifts Vibhishana in a warm embrace and commands Lakshmana to crown him King of Lanka with ocean water on the sand, proving His word is irrevocable.
6. **Scene 6 (CTA Close):** Compact engagement prompt in elevated Hindi.

---

## 3. Visual & World-Building Canon

### Setting & Environment
* **Location:** Northern shoreline of the Southern Ocean (Rameshwaram / Sethu coast).
* **Atmosphere:** Dramatic rolling ocean swells, salt mist in the air, crashing surf against golden sands, distant dark storm clouds over the horizon towards Lanka, divine golden sunlight breaking through clouds onto Sri Rama.
* **Color Palette:** Divine cerulean blue, warm gold, saffron, deep ocean teal, and earthy sandstone.

### Character Bible & Visual Consistency
* **Sri Rama (श्रीराम):**
  * *Complexion & Features:* Radiant dark blue (Shyama-varna), large compassionate lotus-shaped eyes (Rajiv-lochan), dignified gentle smile radiating supreme divinity and Kshatriya majesty.
  * *Attire:* Ascetic saffron/bark robes (*valkala*), simple wooden ornaments and Rudraksha, sacred thread (*yajnopavita*), long flowing black ascetic tresses tied partially in a topknot (*jata*).
  * *Props & Pose:* Holding the divine bow *Kodanda* in His left hand, raising His right hand in the supreme *Abhaya Mudra* (gesture of fearlessness).
* **Vibhishana (विभीषण):**
  * *Appearance:* Noble, tall, dusky-toned Rakshasa prince with refined, serene facial features (not monstrous), wearing modest golden armor, white-and-gold royal dhoti, and folded hands (*Anjali Mudra*).
  * *Posture:* Humbled, prostrated, or kneeling with eyes brimming with tears of devotion (*Bhakti*).
* **Sugriva (सुग्रीव):**
  * *Appearance:* Powerful golden-furred Vanara king, muscular build, wearing a jeweled royal crown and armlets, vigilant tactical stance, gesturing with concerned urgency.
* **Sri Hanuman (हनुमान जी):**
  * *Appearance:* Golden-hued, colossal yet humble Vanara warrior, standing close behind Sri Rama with hands folded in deep reverence and discerning intellect.
* **Lakshmana (लक्ष्मण):**
  * *Appearance:* Fair-complexioned, tall, ascetic archer with fierce devotion to Sri Rama, holding a golden vessel of sea water for the coronation.

---

* **Language Mode:** Pure, elevated, natural spoken Hindi in Devanagari script.
* **Sentence Architecture:** Keep sentences short, rhythmic, and breath-friendly (8–14 words per sentence). Use ample commas and full stops (पूर्णविराम `।`) to guide natural voice pauses for ElevenLabs TTS.
* **Tone:** Epic, inspiring, profound, and deeply devotional.

### Opening & Closing Alignment
* **Exact Opening Line to Use:**  
  *जब रावण के भाई विभीषण ने समुद्र तट पर प्रभु श्री राम से शरण मांगी, तो पूरी वानर सेना स्तब्ध रह गई।*

  Sri Rama’s immortal vow from Valmiki Ramayana that no one who seeks refuge with a sincere heart will ever be rejected—even Ravana himself.
